svg.title: Numbness and tingling are localized first, central or peripheral: a thalamic lesion gives opposite-side clumsiness and burning pain, a spinal cord lesion a truncal sensory level with brisk reflexes, a root a dermatomal pattern with a lost reflex, a mononeuropathy one nerve's territory, a length-dependent polyneuropathy symmetric distal sensory loss, and Guillain-Barre syndrome weakness ascending over days with lost reflexes; each column gives what it looks like, the test that settles it and what to do
